about: Real brand names. The owner's ruling of 27 November 2026 (AGENTS.md: "no real brand only fictional brands that fit into the Jansson world") covers everything in the World, not only what is sold: products, cans, bottles, signs, menus, posters, vehicles, clothes, machines, dialogue, the storyteller and the comics. Two checks read this file. Johansson Studio's checker (src/studio/rules.js) refuses `brands` and `kana` in product, brand and label fields and in a Studio character's name and role. tests/no-real-brands.test.mjs refuses `brands`, `kana` and `contextual` in every piece of text the player or the storyteller can meet (the strings of src/, data/, guide/ and the root content files), except where its allowlist says why a use is not a brand (the night sky's Orion, Asahi as a street, a real place, the credits, a saved game's old name). Where a real brand would fit, use one of the town's own (Umineko, Kame, Shimakaze, Shima TV, the Shisa Drive-In) or the Johansson name, this world's Acme.

copiedFrom.note: That file stays the canonical list for asset kinds and the modeller; this copy began from its 55 and has grown to the owner's ruling of 27 November 2026 (drinks, Okinawa's own brands and distilleries, snacks, shops, tobacco, vehicles, electronics, toys, household names, clothes, papers, broadcasters, teams, airlines). jojo's list should be brought in step with this one (not done from this repository).

kana: キューピーマヨネーズ

contextual.asahi: A brewer, and a street here (Asahi-dōri): the Studio leaves it out (jojo's brandsWhy); the World guard allows it only as the street.
contextual.sapporo: A brewer and a noodle brand, and a city: allowed only as the city or a style of ramen named for it.
contextual.kirin: A brewer, and the mythical beast (and the giraffe): allowed only as the beast or the animal.
contextual.ebisu: Yebisu is a beer; Ebisu is the fishermen's god: allowed only as the god.
contextual.meiji: A confectioner and a dairy, and the Meiji era: allowed only as the era (or a shrine or a road named for it).
contextual.lotte: A confectioner, and a girl's name: allowed only as a person's name.
contextual.morinaga: A confectioner, and a surname: allowed only as a person's name.
contextual.honda: A maker of cars and motorbikes, and a surname: allowed only as a person's name.
contextual.suzuki: A maker of cars and motorbikes, and a common surname (and a fish): allowed only as a person or the fish.
contextual.toyota: A carmaker, and a surname and a city: allowed only as a person or the city.
contextual.kawasaki: A maker of motorbikes and ships, and a city and a surname: allowed only as a person or the city.
contextual.kubota: A maker of tractors and engines, and a surname: allowed only as a person's name.
contextual.mizuno: A maker of sports goods, and a surname: allowed only as a person's name.
contextual.subaru: A carmaker, and the Pleiades: allowed only as the stars.
contextual.seiko: A watchmaker, and a given name: allowed only as a person's name.
contextual.zuisen: An awamori distillery, and the Zuisen gate of Shuri Castle: allowed only as the gate.
contextual.zanpa: An awamori, and Cape Zanpa: allowed only as the cape.
contextual.puma: A maker of sports shoes, and the animal: allowed only in lower case, as the animal.
contextual.sprite: A soda, and a fairy and a graphics term (three.js Sprite): allowed only in lower case or as THREE.Sprite.
contextual.excel: Spreadsheet software, and a verb: allowed only as the verb, in lower case.
contextual.tulip: Okinawa's favourite luncheon meat, and a flower: allowed only as the flower.
contextual.aeon: A supermarket chain, and a word: allowed only as the word, in lower case.

added.orion: jojo's list has only "orion beer", so "Orion lager", "Orion draught" and "Orion, a bottle" slipped through. Orion is a real Okinawan beer.
added.kana: Shelf labels are written in Japanese as often as in English, so the same brands are checked in katakana (and the few written in kanji). Words that are also ordinary words or names here stay out, as in jojo's list: マツダ (also the surname Matsuda) and 日立 (also a city).
added.ruling: 27 November 2026: the owner's ruling made the list cover the whole World. Found and replaced then: Orion on Minato's and Sato Ramen's beer, the bar, the house fridge and the labels (now Umineko, Johansson Brewery's town lager); Zuisen and Kumesen on the bottle keep (Shimakaze); Spam (luncheon meat); A&W (the Shisa Drive-In); Tamagotchi (the Pocket Piyo); NHK (JHK Okinawa); Okinawa TV (Shima TV); the Ryūkyū Shimpō (the Minato Shimbun); the Hawks (the Habus); Purikura (photo-sticker); the Super Cub (the postman's red motorbike); a Washlet (a Johansson bidet seat); thermos (flask); Risograph (Stencil print); Excel (the spreadsheet); IKEA on the furniture's scene names.

leftOut.asahi: Left out on purpose, as in jojo's brandsWhy: Asahi is a street name here.
leftOut.why: Real makers and shops a 1990s Japanese town would show. Words that are also ordinary words or names here are left out on purpose: the onsen's bandai (番台) counter, the Meiji era, Asahi as a street, surnames such as Honda, Suzuki or Toyota, and words like national, sharp, canon or apple.
leftOut.words: Brands that are also everyday words are left to the reader, because no list can tell them apart: national, sharp, canon, citizen, hope, peace, boss, georgia, crown, lion, line, joy, tide, attack, cabin, lark, kent, camel, champion, pioneer, olympus, apple, coco, union, visa, ana. Write them as words, never as a maker.
leftOut.notBrands: Not brands, and kept: formats and media (laserdisc, CD, VHS), the onsen's bandai counter, the Hārī, generic food and drink (awamori, chūhai, ramune, cup noodles (the brand is the singular Cup Noodle), root beer, luncheon meat, written so and never with the tin's brand), and the real places the town is in (Nago, Naha, Kokusai-dōri, Shuri).
leftOut.outsideTheWorld: The owner's own YouTube videos on Minato's television (branch tv/youtube) are embedded through YouTube's player at the owner's request: a real service, not a brand in the World, so "youtube" is not listed.

fields: product.label (every text layer, and every word printed on a picture)
knownIssuesWhy: World's own real-brand uses, each with its file and the words that find it (match; line is only where it was last seen), printed as a warning (validate, publish_check) until it is replaced. Empty since 27 November 2026, when every one was replaced (see added.ruling); tests/no-real-brands.test.mjs keeps it so.
